correctness.rationale: Let z_v=L^dagger e_v and s_k=z_{k+1}-z_k. Because L s_k=e_{k+1}-e_k and s_k has mean zero, s_k is the centered step potential with value -(n-k)/(n w_k) to the left and k/(n w_k) to the right. Direct coordinate multiplication gives the strictly positive Gram entry min(i,j)*(n-max(i,j))/(n w_i w_j). Column-sum zero then gives z_v=P_v-Q_v with positive left/right edge sums, z_1=-(V_v+Q_v), z_n=P_v+U_v. For v<=mid the left endpoint has V_v>=P_v coefficient-wise, making ||z_1||^2-||z_v||^2=||V||^2-||P||^2+2<V+P,Q> strictly positive. For v>=mid the right endpoint gives the reflected strict comparison. n>=3 makes both edge sets nonempty at every interior vertex. Spectral decomposition verifies (L^2)^dagger=(L^dagger)^2, independent of eigenvalue degeneracies.

value.rationale: A natural individual second-order coherence statistic measures noisy-consensus vulnerability or mean squared biharmonic eccentricity. The structural location theorem reduces an arbitrary heterogeneous path worst-node scan to its endpoints and requires an all-weights positive cone argument, not a trace computation or routine first-order effective resistance formula.

limitations: Undirected connected simple path, positive conductances, symmetric unnormalized combinatorial Laplacian, second inverse power only; no conductance optimization.
